documents.title: The artist's guide
documents.description: Your complete workflow, from the first surface to the final refinement.
documents.html:
Start with a layer#

Create a Cyrus Scatter controller, add a layer, assign its receiving surfaces and add models or Points. Set Amount, then press Update scatter in Manual mode. Live responds to relevant edits.

In Geometry > Cyrus > Cyrus Scatter, click to place, move to size the icon, and click to finish. Right-click to exit Create mode. Each layer owns its surfaces, sources, amount, layout, transforms and spacing. Layer order matters when between-layer spacing is enabled.

Use Add, Copy, Remove, Up and Down to organize layers. Copy includes independent Paint Areas. Visible controls viewport display; Enabled controls the layer contribution. Removing an assignment does not delete the source scene object.

In 0.82.6, closed sections create controls on first opening and reuse them while the command panel remains mounted. Switching layers rebinds those controls. Browsing does not apply pending Manual edits.

Surfaces, models and optional containers#

Add receivers to the selected layer. Unchanged receivers retain their base random streams when another receiver is added, renamed or reordered. Density gives each receiver its own count below the cap; Fixed Total redistributes the same total, so some existing candidates may be removed. Geometry changes, Relax, masks and shared spacing can change accepted output.

Add Point makes placement markers without final model geometry. Pick object turns a selected Point into a model. Make point turns a selected model into a Point while preserving its registration, settings and Band assignments; the scene model is not deleted. Both actions preserve the source row identity. An Empty choice creates weighted gaps in Candidate budget mode; positive-weight Empty is rejected by Accepted target. A Point and an Empty are different source kinds.

Source controls include label, identification color, weight, scale, Manual/Auto radius, vertical offset and forward axis. Manual preserves its radius and optional Follow Scale. Auto bounds supported geometry around the pivot after final instance scale and orientation; it is conservative spacing, not exact mesh collision. Points, Empty and unqualified source families remain Manual. Assignment-group colors are separate from identification colors.

Source containers are optional palettes. New rectangles start with Enable collection off. Position and resize first, then enable collection to collect eligible source pivots. Selecting a rectangle opens compact collection and dimension controls; select the Scatter controller for full planting settings. Moving an enabled rectangle carries its owned models; resizing its boundary leaves their transforms unchanged. Disabling collection parks models while retaining settings. Manual waits for Update; Live applies relevant membership changes.

Layout and Amount#

Planting positions chooses Surface random, Rectangular, Staggered or Hexagonal. Grids expose world-unit spacing, fixed Origin X/Y, Heading and stable Jitter. They project down onto the highest receiver hit. Hexagonal calculates row pitch from its nearest-neighbor distance. Count/Density and refill are inactive; masks and collision rules thin the lattice. Source assignment below is independent. Entirely vertical receivers and Analyzer Single/EdgeRow positions are unsupported with grids.

Random mix chooses weighted sources. Clusters choose assignment groups across space. Spline Bands use closed world-XY Paths, explicit Models / Points or Assignment groups, and Consecutive or Independent ranges. Surface Analyzer consumes separately analyzed boundary, path and point channels.

Consecutive accumulates widths separately on each Path/side and preserves unassigned intervals as gaps. Independent exposes each Band's Start/End and combines eligible contributions. New Bands start unassigned. Scaling a Path changes its outline, not its world-space Band distances.

Density and its optional curve shape a Band's contribution from Start to End. Independent contributions cap total occupancy at 100%, then choose the Band proportionally. A 100% Sphere plus 25% Box gives approximately 80% Sphere/20% Box in the overlap and 25% occupancy where only Box contributes, before other masks/spacing.

Rounded uses distance to original border segments. Sharp uses bounded miter offsets; acute corners have limits and narrow/complex requests can require simplification. The preview shows admitted geometry.

Amount supports Count or area Density, up to 1,000,000 per population. A controller shares a 1,000,000-candidate work limit across its populations, including retry and protected-edit requirements. Exceeding that limit reports an error and retains the preceding result. Candidate budget can underfill after restrictions. Independent ranges and nontrivial Band density require Candidate budget; Accepted target is rejected so retries cannot erase the fade. Use a fixed seed for repeatable comparisons. Texture Density uses a selected UV channel (1..99, default 1) on each receiver. Choose 64, 128, 256 or 512 samples per side (default 128). Higher resolution helps capture narrow mask details at a greater preparation cost. UVs clamp to 0..1; white permits and black excludes. Unchanged maps reuse their sampled data across receiver edits. Errors identify the invalid receiver/channel and retain the previous complete result.

0.86.0 keeps placement-sized calculation and storage in native memory. Count changes no longer reserve MAXScript heap proportional to every plant. Undo remains available; a failed successor preserves the last complete result. The one-million controller work limit and memory safeguards remain. Large calculations, complex source geometry and Bake can still block Max while they finish.

Mesh channel density#

In Amount, enable Use mesh channel mask. Channel 0 reads vertex colors; channels 1..99 read numbered mesh map channels from the evaluated receiver. Choose R/X, G/Y or B/Z to match the component written by Data Channel or VertexPaint. Every assigned receiver needs that channel.

For terrain curvature, place Data Channel above the deformation, add Curvature, then Vertex Output to an unused Map Channel and component X. Select the same channel and R/X in Scatter. The rainbow display colors are visualization; planting reads stored numeric values. Curvature describes bending, while slope describes steepness.

Input min/max map the chosen values into 0..1 and clamp outside values. Min must be below max. Invert reverses the normalized value before the Density curve: 0 excludes plants, 1 permits them, and gray values thin stable candidates. Triangle map-face interpolation respects channel seams. The mask has mesh detail rather than a sampled bitmap resolution.

The mask combines with texture density, slope/altitude and Paint without creating Paint strokes. It runs after candidate movement/Relax and before CS Edit. Masked base edits remain dormant until eligibility returns; existing explicitly moved or cloned protected edits follow the established replay rules. Channel-only changes preserve geometry bindings. Nonzero movement requires Keep on surface.

Preview mask reads current inputs into at most 2,048 grayscale face-centre markers across the layer. It shows only this mask and may differ from pending Manual plants. Relevant edits clear the snapshot; click Preview again to refresh, or Hide preview to clear it. Redraw uses cached markers without channel reads. Each receiver supports up to two million evaluated faces; VData, selection and negative map channels are outside this version.

Manual waits for Update scatter; Live follows relevant channel/modifier edits and animation. Missing or invalid channels identify the receiver and retain the previous complete result. The layer owns its mask and curve, and copied layers retain independent settings. Named presets for this new curve are not available in this version.

Band scale profiles#

In Layout, Scale sits directly below the density curve. Min/Max supplies random size variation. Scale profile selects Off, Follow Density or Custom. Custom enables Edit scale curve. X runs from Band Start to End; Y is size percent, where 100% preserves size.

Density and scale have independent curves. Follow Density uses the effective density curve shape, without the Density % strength; disabling that density curve gives a flat 100% scale profile. Switching modes keeps the Custom graph. Zero size does not remove a candidate.

Scale curves multiply existing source, Band and layer size once. Auto Radius follows final size; Manual radius needs Follow Scale. Size-dependent spacing can change accepted counts. Manual requires Update scatter. Steep Sharp profiles can exceed the bounded precision and retain the previous result; simplify the curve or choose Rounded.

Slope and altitude filters#

Enable Filter slope or Filter altitude in Include / exclude areas ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ Surface eligibility. Slope is measured from world up using the evaluated geometric normal: 0Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â° upward, 90Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â° vertical, 180Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â° downward. Altitude is world Z at the final receiver anchor, before source pivot offsets.

Lower and Upper fade soften density inside the range. For a 0ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Å“35Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â° slope interval, a 10Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â° upper fade thins between 25Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â° and 35Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â°. Zero fade includes the endpoint. Fades cannot overlap; invalid settings retain the previous complete result.

Filters preserve surviving candidate IDs, model choices and transforms. Paint overlap still uses max-union density; explicitly moved or cloned CS Edit plants bypass these filters. Spacing and cleanup follow filtering. Use Candidate budget to retain the visible density fade; Accepted target can refill within its finite work budget.

Manual waits for Update; Live follows relevant edits and receiver animation. The status describes the last calculated prepared pool, separately from accepted plants. Heights use scene units and survive scene-unit conversion.

Named settings and curve presets#

Use Presets... in Amount, Transforms or Spacing & cleanup. Curve presets are available from Paint, Analyzer and Band density/scale graphs. Save new captures a named item; selecting it is passive, and Apply changes the target shown in the dialog. Reopen the browser to target a different layer.

Population includes amount, density, seed and retry policy. Transforms include the layer rotation, scale, movement, normal alignment and projection. Assets, surfaces, IDs, maps and layout remain linked to the scene. Physical distances convert across system units; density stays per square metre.

Spacing stores the effective rule and applies an explicit override in the chosen Within this layer or Between layers scope. It does not store peer identities or change Relax/cleanup. Reset inheritance remains a separate control.

Curve presets preserve samples and editable handles while retaining enable flags, widths and scale ranges. Density and Paint scale use zero-to-one values; other scale curves support multipliers. Invalid or incompatible curves are rejected. One Undo/Redo restores Apply, and closing a graph after Undo does not reapply the preset.

Manual waits for Update scatter; Live follows normal update callbacks. Browsing, saving and renaming do not calculate plants. Animated or expression-controlled targets are rejected. Static shared controllers are detached so another owner is preserved.

The local library is CyrusScatter/Presets inside the per-user Max PlugCFG directory. Share the .cspreset.json files. Limits are 512 files, 64 KiB per file and 80-character names. Rename changes the library name; Delete confirms removal of the selected file. Invalid files and failed writes report errors. Complete static recipes and explicit role substitution are available through Layers > Recipes.

Vector painting#

Turn on Use Paint Areas, add a named area and choose one receiver from the layer. Select Paint or Erase, set Radius and press Start Brush. Paint joins circular footprints into a vector region; Erase cuts coverage and holes. Stop ends the session.

Areas share the layer models and population. Overlap contributes coverage once per candidate. Turning Paint Areas off retains the areas and uses the full receiver. Fill and Clear operate on the selected area; keep a saved copy before major edits.

Inward/outward feather widths and separate density/scale curves shape the edge. Density changes acceptance; scale multiplies model size. A 100 mm radius has a 200 mm diameter. Borders describe coverage, not guaranteed accepted plants.

Hover over Paint controls for short descriptions. Fade density changes plant acceptance; Fade scale changes size independently. Inside and Outside fade define the transition width. With the default curve, Edge scale is the outer-end size multiplier and Inner scale is the interior multiplier: 0.5 means half size, 1 unchanged and 2 double. Edge scale cannot exceed Inner scale. The graph shapes the transition between them.

Vector painting supports planes and terrain single-valued in receiver-local XY, including transformed receivers. Closed, vertical, folded and overlapping projected receivers are rejected. General scattering on curved receivers is a separate supported workflow.

The vector format introduced in 0.78 does not convert earlier stroke setups. Preserve older scenes with their matching build and create a new setup for the vector workflow.

Paint and spline snapshots#

Stop the brush and select a Paint Area. Export spline creates and selects an independent Editable Spline with its closed contours and holes. Edit the border in Max, reselect the Scatter and Paint Area, choose Replace or Add, then press Pick spline... and choose the shape. Escape cancels picking.

Export uses the receiver's local XY plane at local Z=0 with its scene transform. On terrain the spline is a planar editing guide. Import projects along receiver-local Z, clips to the receiver and requires every contour to be closed. Nested loops and self-intersections use even-odd fill regardless of winding or order.

Replace sets coverage; Add unions it with the existing region without erasing paint. Density, fades, models and area identity stay unchanged. A changed import and each export are one Undo. Manual waits for Update; Live follows changed coverage. There is no live source link: later spline edits require another import.

Curve tolerance is a world-unit approximation distance, initially 1 mm. Smaller values need more samples. A shape is limited to 8,192 input knots and 8,192 sampled vertices. Paint precision imposes a minimum tolerance; very large local coordinates can prevent accurate Max spline export. Invalid conversion retains existing paint. Reopen using the saved scene units; native Paint geometry conversion guards still apply.

Area limits, transforms and spacing#

Closed Include shapes union their eligible domains. Exclude takes precedence. Area masks test placement support rather than trimming model geometry. Layout & soft boundaries explains guide widths and edge curves.

Rotation, XYZ scale, whole scale and movement have independent ranges and reset buttons. Projection and orientation settings affect final placement. Within-layer and between-layer spacing are independent rules; radius, factor, gap and Follow Scale determine simplified clearance.

CS Edit uses stable instance identities. Generation changes can invalidate bindings; preserve the scene before clearing edits. Radius overlays are inspection aids, not exact mesh collision volumes.

Preview, updates, output and diagnostics#

Plant centres shows one marker per accepted placement. Point Cloud, Proxy and Mesh have their own display budgets, so shown counts can be lower than accepted output. Mesh uses evaluated viewport geometry and preview coloring; renderer materials are a separate output concern.

Color by Bands follows the accepted owner even when Bands share a model. Preview Falloff shows selected contribution or Combined density on receiver surfaces: blue is zero and red is 100%. Show Boundaries adds white contours. Sample/face counts describe approximate coverage at the Band stage before other masks, spacing and cleanup. These overlays are not final plants or render output.

Manual retains the last completed result until Update scatter. Live updates relevant dependencies. A failed successor retains the previous complete result and reports the failure. If an Analyzer is stale, Analyze it first and then update Manual Scatter.

In Manual, enabled field feedback follows relevant authored/animated inputs while published plants and radii stay frozen. The label reads Pending field; plants from last Update. Field toggles, selection and XY/3D radius display do not solve placements. An uncached display mode cannot use changed source geometry alongside the preceding publication; Update is required.

Local identification-color edits retain unchanged sibling previews. Unchanged navigation reuses prepared display data. Heavy changed layers, cold loading and first panel construction can still take time.

Statistics identifies the selected layer and its last completed calculation. Requested and accepted placements are separate from prepared cloud points, centres or preview instances. Prepared samples are not current-frame draw counts. Marked for Update reports pending invalidation; Read cached statistics does not apply Manual edits. Empty successful results and failed updates have separate feedback. Optional diagnostics record local bounded events; recording is separate from sharing or permission to train.

In Viewport & render, Navigating and Idle set separate limits for Point Cloud points, Proxy instances or Mesh triangles across visible layers. Use 0 for unlimited. A short pause restores Idle detail; final rendering retains the full accepted planting. Expensive Mesh sources can use cached boxes to fit the triangle or memory allowance. Oversized Point Cloud requests use a bounded sample and report the memory reduction, including at zero limits; switching modes reuses the current planting snapshots. Zero removes artist draw caps but keeps memory safeguards. Graphics failure uses bounded centre markers. Display changes preserve pending Manual edits.

From 0.82.6, saved reports include call counts, total time, longest time and failed-stage counts for input extraction, candidates, masks, transforms/radii, spacing, preview preparation, uploads, publication and panel work. Times are inclusive: a parent can contain another measured stage, so do not add all totals together. Action IDs connect an edit to invalidation and its deferred publication; unrelated host activity can have no action ID. The selected-setup snapshot reads cached requested/accepted/prepared counts and pending flags without evaluating the scene. These timings do not measure presented viewport FPS.

Final artist acceptance#

Use the qualified 0.85.3 Max 2027 MZP through Scripting > Run Script, or the companion Windows EXE, then restart Max so script and native modules match. The EXE is unsigned and uses Windows .NET Framework 4.8. Personal recipes and activation are preserved. Neither route starts or restarts Max for you.

Team-pilot builds expose License / activation. Export an activation request and import the returned license. The pilot license lasts 30 days from issuance; expiry locks authoring while existing scenes remain loadable/renderable.

Development source 0.85.3 uses schema 58; earlier schemas are rejected without migration. Preserve earlier scenes with their matching build. Current settings use typed distances. Preserve originals and use saved units for receiver-bound Paint/Edit data. Test receivers, Points/models, Bands, painting, mesh-channel masks, Manual/Live, Undo/Redo, save/reopen and the intended renderer on a copy. Physical picker/DPI/tablet and production-session acceptance remain open.

View the changelog for additions and fixes, or use the testing walkthrough to record your own observations.

Complete planting recipes#

Open Layers > Recipes for the collection tree and large thumbnail gallery. Choose My recipes, Bundled examples or a custom library. Open a collection or choose All recipes; search names, layers, tags and descriptions. The toolbar controls thumbnail/list view and tile size. Refresh explicitly rereads files; ordinary browsing does not calculate plants or capture images.

Save Recipe saves selected layers, names, collections, tags, description, optional thumbnail and complete supported native Paint. Include models, materials, terrain and paths is checked by default for a ready preset. Terrain is an evaluated geometry/channel snapshot, not an editable modifier stack. Captured references exclude unrelated same-name objects. Saving pending Manual settings does not calculate plants. My recipes is Documents/CyrusScatter/Library; bundled examples remain separate.

Use a PNG up to 1024 pixels per axis and 2 MiB, or explicitly capture the published viewport. A stale preview after a Manual edit requires a valid capture choice; Update-and-capture runs only when requested. Update selected advances the recipe revision, Save Copy creates another identity, and Edit details changes presentation without touching the scene. Keep the manifest and all referenced recipe-data payloads together when copying.

Load + Update loads a ready preset with its supported models/materials and adds new layers. Existing planting and Manual/Live mode are retained. An unambiguous compatible current terrain is used; required Paint, channel or spline context can use included terrain, clearly reported. The explicit Update also applies pending Manual edits. Delayed node notifications settle before the one final solve. One Undo/Redo restores complete publication and imported ownership.

Paint requires compatible receiver geometry, frame and saved units. Unsupported authored Edit/per-instance radius records and parameter controllers reject complete save rather than being omitted. There is no automatic Paint projection onto an unrelated mountain. Memory admission can reject an operation while preserving the previous complete result and history; arbitrary heavy-session reliability remains separate acceptance.

Apply Style copies chosen supported setting groups to a captured layer, retaining its receivers, sources and Paint by default. Keep/Saved/New variation and explicit map/target bindings are reviewed. Applying identical effective values creates no additional Undo or calculation.

Export portable package collects permitted static standalone meshes, supported Standard/Blinn materials and static PNG maps, along with recipe and Paint data. Bind external terrain/path roles on import. Create independent assets or explicitly reuse chosen scene models with their current materials. Reuse transfers no ownership. XRefs, nested populations, renderer-specific proxies/shaders and material-variant browsing are outside this adapter.

Eight examples provide editable scenes and actual-result previews: meadow, woodland, mountain, painted spline borders, orchard, hexagonal hillside, four garden rooms and valley moss/rocky crests. Open a copy of a matching scene for compatible bindings. The new valley example uses authored numeric mesh-channel data, not a new automatic curvature engine.

For a settings-only recipe or deliberate substitution, use Recipe actions > Review bindings (advanced). Ready metadata revisions retain their asset linkage. Keep the recipe-data payloads and Presets/<recipe content identity> package folder together when copying a ready library. The eight bundled presets use original procedural demonstration models; unsupported XRefs, animated dependencies, renderer-specific proxies/shaders and authored Edit/radius data remain separate work.

Direction and normal blending#

In Transforms > Orientation, choose Random, World direction or Look at target. World direction aims along a nonzero XYZ vector. Look at target aims toward a picked objectÃ¢â‚¬â„¢s world pivot. Models use local +Z up and the Forward axis set in Models & Points. Local random rotations still apply; zero their ranges to check exact aim.

Align to normal and Normal % set preferred up: disabled or 0% uses world +Z; 100% uses the geometric face normal, with angular blending between. Direction modes use this to control roll while preserving heading. Slope eligibility is independent. Coincident targets and parallel heading/up use deterministic fallbacks.

Manual waits for Update. Live follows relevant target/parent or orientation animation. Missing targets and zero vectors retain the last complete plants and report failure. Editing the targetÃ¢â‚¬â„¢s shape or rotating it around an unchanged pivot does not calculate scatter.

Complete recipes bind orientation targets as external roles. Numeric Transform presets preserve the destination target and require it for Look at target. New complete recipes use format 5 and numeric settings presets use format 3. Grid distances convert with scene units; earlier complete formats receive neutral Surface random defaults. Complete recipe formats 1/2 retain original receiver random inputs when read; format 1 also receives neutral orientation defaults. Reading never rewrites Paint or files. Physical picker, 4K and mixed-monitor testing remains artist acceptance.

Copy and import variation#

Choose Same variation (default) or New variation before copying a layer. Both create independent layer ownership and Paint. Same retains receiver random inputs; New chooses fresh inputs once. Changing the choice is passive.

Recipes default to New variation. Choose Saved variation to retain the saved random inputs, then Add layers or Create new setup. Exact matching requires identical evaluated terrain, receiver history, quotas, source order/weights, masks, Relax and collision context. Paint requires compatible geometry, frame and saved units.

Amount settings presets separately offer Saved seed, Keep current seed or New seed. These numeric presets do not contain complete arrangements. Redo restores the chosen variation rather than rerolling.

Named layer Copy currently rejects authored Scatter Edit and per-instance radius data; use Max object Copy for a complete setup. The native foundation preserves tested Count/copy/preset/Edit history without full script placement arrays. Resource rejection retains the previous complete result. Arbitrary low-memory conditions and sustained artist production acceptance remain separate.

search.title: Named settings and curve presets
search.text: Use Presets... in Amount, Transforms or Spacing & cleanup. Curve presets are available from Paint, Analyzer and Band density/scale graphs. Save new captures a named item; selecting it is passive, and Apply changes the target shown in the dialog. Reopen the browser to target a different layer.

search.title: Named settings and curve presets
search.text: Population includes amount, density, seed and retry policy. Transforms include the layer rotation, scale, movement, normal alignment and projection. Assets, surfaces, IDs, maps and layout remain linked to the scene. Physical distances convert across system units; density stays per square metre.

search.title: Named settings and curve presets
search.text: Spacing stores the effective rule and applies an explicit override in the chosen Within this layer or Between layers scope. It does not store peer identities or change Relax/cleanup. Reset inheritance remains a separate control.

search.title: Named settings and curve presets
search.text: Curve presets preserve samples and editable handles while retaining enable flags, widths and scale ranges. Density and Paint scale use zero-to-one values; other scale curves support multipliers. Invalid or incompatible curves are rejected. One Undo/Redo restores Apply, and closing a graph after Undo does not reapply the preset.

search.title: Named settings and curve presets
search.text: Manual waits for Update scatter; Live follows normal update callbacks. Browsing, saving and renaming do not calculate plants. Animated or expression-controlled targets are rejected. Static shared controllers are detached so another owner is preserved.

search.title: Named settings and curve presets
search.text: The local library is CyrusScatter/Presets inside the per-user Max PlugCFG directory. Share the .cspreset.json files. Limits are 512 files, 64 KiB per file and 80-character names. Rename changes the library name; Delete confirms removal of the selected file. Invalid files and failed writes report errors. Complete static recipes and explicit role substitution are available through Layers > Recipes.

search.title: Vector painting
search.text: Turn on Use Paint Areas, add a named area and choose one receiver from the layer. Select Paint or Erase, set Radius and press Start Brush. Paint joins circular footprints into a vector region; Erase cuts coverage and holes. Stop ends the session.

search.title: Vector painting
search.text: Areas share the layer models and population. Overlap contributes coverage once per candidate. Turning Paint Areas off retains the areas and uses the full receiver. Fill and Clear operate on the selected area; keep a saved copy before major edits.

search.title: Vector painting
search.text: Inward/outward feather widths and separate density/scale curves shape the edge. Density changes acceptance; scale multiplies model size. A 100 mm radius has a 200 mm diameter. Borders describe coverage, not guaranteed accepted plants.

search.title: Vector painting
search.text: Hover over Paint controls for short descriptions. Fade density changes plant acceptance; Fade scale changes size independently. Inside and Outside fade define the transition width. With the default curve, Edge scale is the outer-end size multiplier and Inner scale is the interior multiplier: 0.5 means half size, 1 unchanged and 2 double. Edge scale cannot exceed Inner scale. The graph shapes the transition between them.

search.title: Vector painting
search.text: Vector painting supports planes and terrain single-valued in receiver-local XY, including transformed receivers. Closed, vertical, folded and overlapping projected receivers are rejected. General scattering on curved receivers is a separate supported workflow.

search.title: Vector painting
search.text: The vector format introduced in 0.78 does not convert earlier stroke setups. Preserve older scenes with their matching build and create a new setup for the vector workflow.

search.title: Paint and spline snapshots
search.text: Stop the brush and select a Paint Area. Export spline creates and selects an independent Editable Spline with its closed contours and holes. Edit the border in Max, reselect the Scatter and Paint Area, choose Replace or Add, then press Pick spline... and choose the shape. Escape cancels picking.

search.title: Paint and spline snapshots
search.text: Export uses the receiver's local XY plane at local Z=0 with its scene transform. On terrain the spline is a planar editing guide. Import projects along receiver-local Z, clips to the receiver and requires every contour to be closed. Nested loops and self-intersections use even-odd fill regardless of winding or order.

search.title: Paint and spline snapshots
search.text: Replace sets coverage; Add unions it with the existing region without erasing paint. Density, fades, models and area identity stay unchanged. A changed import and each export are one Undo. Manual waits for Update; Live follows changed coverage. There is no live source link: later spline edits require another import.

search.title: Paint and spline snapshots
search.text: Curve tolerance is a world-unit approximation distance, initially 1 mm. Smaller values need more samples. A shape is limited to 8,192 input knots and 8,192 sampled vertices. Paint precision imposes a minimum tolerance; very large local coordinates can prevent accurate Max spline export. Invalid conversion retains existing paint. Reopen using the saved scene units; native Paint geometry conversion guards still apply.

search.title: Area limits, transforms and spacing
search.text: Closed Include shapes union their eligible domains. Exclude takes precedence. Area masks test placement support rather than trimming model geometry. Layout & soft boundaries explains guide widths and edge curves.

search.title: Area limits, transforms and spacing
search.text: Rotation, XYZ scale, whole scale and movement have independent ranges and reset buttons. Projection and orientation settings affect final placement. Within-layer and between-layer spacing are independent rules; radius, factor, gap and Follow Scale determine simplified clearance.

search.title: Area limits, transforms and spacing
search.text: CS Edit uses stable instance identities. Generation changes can invalidate bindings; preserve the scene before clearing edits. Radius overlays are inspection aids, not exact mesh collision volumes.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: Plant centres shows one marker per accepted placement. Point Cloud, Proxy and Mesh have their own display budgets, so shown counts can be lower than accepted output. Mesh uses evaluated viewport geometry and preview coloring; renderer materials are a separate output concern.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: Color by Bands follows the accepted owner even when Bands share a model. Preview Falloff shows selected contribution or Combined density on receiver surfaces: blue is zero and red is 100%. Show Boundaries adds white contours. Sample/face counts describe approximate coverage at the Band stage before other masks, spacing and cleanup. These overlays are not final plants or render output.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: Manual retains the last completed result until Update scatter. Live updates relevant dependencies. A failed successor retains the previous complete result and reports the failure. If an Analyzer is stale, Analyze it first and then update Manual Scatter.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: In Manual, enabled field feedback follows relevant authored/animated inputs while published plants and radii stay frozen. The label reads Pending field; plants from last Update. Field toggles, selection and XY/3D radius display do not solve placements. An uncached display mode cannot use changed source geometry alongside the preceding publication; Update is required.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: Local identification-color edits retain unchanged sibling previews. Unchanged navigation reuses prepared display data. Heavy changed layers, cold loading and first panel construction can still take time.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: Statistics identifies the selected layer and its last completed calculation. Requested and accepted placements are separate from prepared cloud points, centres or preview instances. Prepared samples are not current-frame draw counts. Marked for Update reports pending invalidation; Read cached statistics does not apply Manual edits. Empty successful results and failed updates have separate feedback. Optional diagnostics record local bounded events; recording is separate from sharing or permission to train.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: In Viewport & render, Navigating and Idle set separate limits for Point Cloud points, Proxy instances or Mesh triangles across visible layers. Use 0 for unlimited. A short pause restores Idle detail; final rendering retains the full accepted planting. Expensive Mesh sources can use cached boxes to fit the triangle or memory allowance. Oversized Point Cloud requests use a bounded sample and report the memory reduction, including at zero limits; switching modes reuses the current planting snapshots. Zero removes artist draw caps but keeps memory safeguards. Graphics failure uses bounded centre markers. Display changes preserve pending Manual edits.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: From 0.82.6, saved reports include call counts, total time, longest time and failed-stage counts for input extraction, candidates, masks, transforms/radii, spacing, preview preparation, uploads, publication and panel work. Times are inclusive: a parent can contain another measured stage, so do not add all totals together. Action IDs connect an edit to invalidation and its deferred publication; unrelated host activity can have no action ID. The selected-setup snapshot reads cached requested/accepted/prepared counts and pending flags without evaluating the scene. These timings do not measure presented viewport FPS.

search.title: Final artist acceptance
search.text: Use the qualified 0.85.3 Max 2027 MZP through Scripting > Run Script, or the companion Windows EXE, then restart Max so script and native modules match. The EXE is unsigned and uses Windows .NET Framework 4.8. Personal recipes and activation are preserved. Neither route starts or restarts Max for you.

search.title: Final artist acceptance
search.text: Team-pilot builds expose License / activation. Export an activation request and import the returned license. The pilot license lasts 30 days from issuance; expiry locks authoring while existing scenes remain loadable/renderable.

search.title: Final artist acceptance
search.text: Development source 0.85.3 uses schema 58; earlier schemas are rejected without migration. Preserve earlier scenes with their matching build. Current settings use typed distances. Preserve originals and use saved units for receiver-bound Paint/Edit data. Test receivers, Points/models, Bands, painting, mesh-channel masks, Manual/Live, Undo/Redo, save/reopen and the intended renderer on a copy. Physical picker/DPI/tablet and production-session acceptance remain open.

search.title: Final artist acceptance
search.text: View the changelog for additions and fixes, or use the testing walkthrough to record your own observations.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Open Layers > Recipes for the collection tree and large thumbnail gallery. Choose My recipes, Bundled examples or a custom library. Open a collection or choose All recipes; search names, layers, tags and descriptions. The toolbar controls thumbnail/list view and tile size. Refresh explicitly rereads files; ordinary browsing does not calculate plants or capture images.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Save Recipe saves selected layers, names, collections, tags, description, optional thumbnail and complete supported native Paint. Include models, materials, terrain and paths is checked by default for a ready preset. Terrain is an evaluated geometry/channel snapshot, not an editable modifier stack. Captured references exclude unrelated same-name objects. Saving pending Manual settings does not calculate plants. My recipes is Documents/CyrusScatter/Library; bundled examples remain separate.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Use a PNG up to 1024 pixels per axis and 2 MiB, or explicitly capture the published viewport. A stale preview after a Manual edit requires a valid capture choice; Update-and-capture runs only when requested. Update selected advances the recipe revision, Save Copy creates another identity, and Edit details changes presentation without touching the scene. Keep the manifest and all referenced recipe-data payloads together when copying.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Load + Update loads a ready preset with its supported models/materials and adds new layers. Existing planting and Manual/Live mode are retained. An unambiguous compatible current terrain is used; required Paint, channel or spline context can use included terrain, clearly reported. The explicit Update also applies pending Manual edits. Delayed node notifications settle before the one final solve. One Undo/Redo restores complete publication and imported ownership.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Paint requires compatible receiver geometry, frame and saved units. Unsupported authored Edit/per-instance radius records and parameter controllers reject complete save rather than being omitted. There is no automatic Paint projection onto an unrelated mountain. Memory admission can reject an operation while preserving the previous complete result and history; arbitrary heavy-session reliability remains separate acceptance.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Apply Style copies chosen supported setting groups to a captured layer, retaining its receivers, sources and Paint by default. Keep/Saved/New variation and explicit map/target bindings are reviewed. Applying identical effective values creates no additional Undo or calculation.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Export portable package collects permitted static standalone meshes, supported Standard/Blinn materials and static PNG maps, along with recipe and Paint data. Bind external terrain/path roles on import. Create independent assets or explicitly reuse chosen scene models with their current materials. Reuse transfers no ownership. XRefs, nested populations, renderer-specific proxies/shaders and material-variant browsing are outside this adapter.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Eight examples provide editable scenes and actual-result previews: meadow, woodland, mountain, painted spline borders, orchard, hexagonal hillside, four garden rooms and valley moss/rocky crests. Open a copy of a matching scene for compatible bindings. The new valley example uses authored numeric mesh-channel data, not a new automatic curvature engine.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: For a settings-only recipe or deliberate substitution, use Recipe actions > Review bindings (advanced). Ready metadata revisions retain their asset linkage. Keep the recipe-data payloads and Presets/<recipe content identity> package folder together when copying a ready library. The eight bundled presets use original procedural demonstration models; unsupported XRefs, animated dependencies, renderer-specific proxies/shaders and authored Edit/radius data remain separate work.

search.title: Direction and normal blending
search.text: In Transforms > Orientation, choose Random, World direction or Look at target. World direction aims along a nonzero XYZ vector. Look at target aims toward a picked objectÃ¢â‚¬â„¢s world pivot. Models use local +Z up and the Forward axis set in Models & Points. Local random rotations still apply; zero their ranges to check exact aim.

search.title: Direction and normal blending
search.text: Align to normal and Normal % set preferred up: disabled or 0% uses world +Z; 100% uses the geometric face normal, with angular blending between. Direction modes use this to control roll while preserving heading. Slope eligibility is independent. Coincident targets and parallel heading/up use deterministic fallbacks.

search.title: Direction and normal blending
search.text: Manual waits for Update. Live follows relevant target/parent or orientation animation. Missing targets and zero vectors retain the last complete plants and report failure. Editing the targetÃ¢â‚¬â„¢s shape or rotating it around an unchanged pivot does not calculate scatter.

search.title: Direction and normal blending
search.text: Complete recipes bind orientation targets as external roles. Numeric Transform presets preserve the destination target and require it for Look at target. New complete recipes use format 5 and numeric settings presets use format 3. Grid distances convert with scene units; earlier complete formats receive neutral Surface random defaults. Complete recipe formats 1/2 retain original receiver random inputs when read; format 1 also receives neutral orientation defaults. Reading never rewrites Paint or files. Physical picker, 4K and mixed-monitor testing remains artist acceptance.

search.title: Copy and import variation
search.text: Choose Same variation (default) or New variation before copying a layer. Both create independent layer ownership and Paint. Same retains receiver random inputs; New chooses fresh inputs once. Changing the choice is passive.

search.title: Copy and import variation
search.text: Recipes default to New variation. Choose Saved variation to retain the saved random inputs, then Add layers or Create new setup. Exact matching requires identical evaluated terrain, receiver history, quotas, source order/weights, masks, Relax and collision context. Paint requires compatible geometry, frame and saved units.

search.title: Copy and import variation
search.text: Amount settings presets separately offer Saved seed, Keep current seed or New seed. These numeric presets do not contain complete arrangements. Redo restores the chosen variation rather than rerolling.

search.title: Copy and import variation
search.text: Named layer Copy currently rejects authored Scatter Edit and per-instance radius data; use Max object Copy for a complete setup. The native foundation preserves tested Count/copy/preset/Edit history without full script placement arrays. Resource rejection retains the previous complete result. Arbitrary low-memory conditions and sustained artist production acceptance remain separate.

documents.title: Layout & soft boundaries
documents.description: Assignment, spline bands, Analyzer guides and the details of falloff.
documents.html:
Assignment and guides#

Grid planting and model assignment are independent. Rectangular, Staggered and Hexagonal use a fixed world XY frame and highest-hit surface projection. Spacing sets population; masks, Paint and collision rules remove cells without random refill. Stable cell identities do not shift with terrain bounds. Analyzer Single/EdgeRow cannot also supply positions to a grid.

Random mix uses model weights; Clusters chooses assignment groups. Spline Bands use closed world-XY Paths and explicit Models / Points or assignment-group choices. Consecutive uses ordered first-match ownership, including empty reserved intervals. Independent combines eligible Band contributions over shared candidates.

Consecutive widths accumulate separately on each side. Two 200 mm inside bands form 0-200 and 200-400 mm strips. Scaling or rotating a spline transforms its outline before distance is measured; it does not scale the width setting.

Independent Start/End ranges may overlap. Density strength multiplies the sampled curve from the near to far boundary, inward for Inside Bands. Contributions sum to capped occupancy, then select a Band proportionally. Independent/nontrivial density requires Candidate budget. Rounded and bounded Sharp joins are explicit Path choices.

Analyzer assignment consumes cached boundary, street, centre-line or point data. Assignment, Analyzer Area masks and boundary falloff have separate Analyzer references. Analyze stale inputs before updating Scatter.

Boundary and street controls#

Face outward uses the source Forward axis. Corner blending changes facing near adjacent edges; hole boundaries face into the hole. Edge Border supports ordered rows, row spacing, jitter, protected corner samples and local XYZ rotation.

Local offsets follow the resulting orientation. They do not resample an inset boundary or guarantee the entire model stays inside. Keep on surface has its own role.

Street Trim shortens connected chains in their traversal direction. Closed loops have no ends to trim. Centre-line Street offset shifts in world XY: positive away, negative toward the nearest street. It requires street data.

Masks and falloff#

Include domains union; Exclude overrides. Analyzer centre-line bands and point discs may union as a mask. Full width is the complete band width. Point radius here differs from source collision radius.

New area rows start as Include. Multi-row selection shows mixed modes explicitly. Choose exactly one Area spline or an Analyzer boundary as the falloff target. Delete width removes an edge strip; density and scale ramps follow that strip when deletion is enabled.

The curve graph uses normalized distance on X and percentage on Y. Density thins acceptance; scale can exceed 100%. Endpoint values apply beyond the ramp. Multiple falloffs can multiply scale and accumulate deletion. Graph edits commit immediately; Close is not Cancel.

Use the scene saved system units. Cross-system-unit conversion of serialized per-area fade distances remains a known limitation.

Edit and preview distinctions#

CS Edit binds stable instance identities rather than row order. Missing or suspended identities are not silently reassigned. Preserve edits before changing generation settings.

Preview budgets and representation do not reduce the accepted population. Point placeholders have no final model geometry until replaced. Empty sources represent weighted gaps. Review source and radius controls.

Band identification follows accepted ownership. Field samples and boundary lines describe the pre-mask Band stage on actual receiver surfaces. Manual feedback explicitly labels pending field edits while preserving completed plants and radii. Auto Radius uses final-basis pivot-centered XY/3D bounds; the radius display metric does not alter spacing rules.

documents.title: Surface Analyzer
documents.description: Understand boundaries, paths, point spacing and planar analysis.
documents.html:
Controls#

Surface Analyzer is a separately versioned companion (0.14). Assign a supported planar mesh and use Analyze to publish boundary, centre-line, street and sample-point guides.

Choose Auto or a method override; configure fit radius, point spacing, count limits, relaxation and analysis resolution. Higher resolution increases precision and work. Manual waits for Analyze; Real-time responds to relevant changes.

Elements, geometry and results#

Edge-connected mesh elements are analyzed independently. Separate planar elements may have different orientations or heights; holes remain part of their element. Weld vertices to join topology. Nonplanar elements, closed solids and invalid boundaries are rejected.

Auto chooses a straight region, radial ring or branched path heuristically. Raster resolution can miss narrow features; eligible regions need not receive complete coverage. Fit radius limits point-centre clearance and spacing can leave branches empty.

Surface area sums world-space triangle areas rather than unioning overlaps. Region area is a mode-dependent feasible-area estimate. Path is total guide length.

Output and persistence#

Relevant edits mark guides pending. Analyze refreshes them. Current/pending state and settings survive save/reopen. Matching Scatter rejects stale linked guides while retaining its last completed output.

Exported splines/helpers are independent snapshots. Cached overlay toggles do not rerun analysis. Analyzer supports separately oriented planar elements; the Scatter adapter for path bands and point masks evaluates in world XY.

Build and checks#

Install the matching Max-year package and restart Max. Source meshes remain unchanged. Large meshes, many elements or high analysis resolution can still pause the UI because analysis is synchronous.

Test holes, attached elements, narrow branches, fit radius, Manual/Real-time and save/reopen on a copy. Read troubleshooting & limits before interpreting an empty result.

documents.title: Product & AI direction
documents.description: What works today, what is experimental and what comes next.
documents.html:
The product today#

The main product is artist-controlled scattering in 3ds Max: layers, receivers, models and Points, optional vector Paint Areas, layouts, area limits, transforms, spacing, previews and exact output. AI is optional and separate.

Development source 0.85.1 adds a collection/thumbnail gallery, explicit preview capture, revisioned recipe saving, selective style, bounded static mesh/material/PNG packages and explicit scene-model reuse. Eight procedural examples and MZP/EXE distribution are included in the 0.85.1 development delivery. Qualification uses Max 2027 only; see the handoff for exact evidence and limits. XRefs, nested populations, renderer-specific adapters and authored Edit/effect presets remain separate work. Physical input, mixed-monitor DPI and production renderer/session acceptance are not implied.

Assistant access today#

The separate MCP foundation supports cached inspection and a smaller approved authoring subset. A feature appearing in the local control catalog does not mean an assistant can invoke it.

Current MCP does not provide full vector painting, arbitrary artist-scene editing or automatic renderer execution. Read the MCP guide for scope and approval boundaries.

Learning foundations today#

An offline experimental ranker explores bounded alternatives. It is not a production reference-image designer or a personal artist-trained model. Local diagnostic recording, assistant sharing and training consent are separate choices.

Roadmap#

The stages below describe direction, not delivery dates or promises. Each stage needs a useful artist workflow and independent acceptance.

1. Qualify the everyday artist workflow#

Complete physical picker, brush, curve, DPI and tablet testing; strengthen system-unit conversion, long sessions, renderer lifecycle and install/recovery coverage.

2. Broaden MCP through complete artist tasks#

Expand supported tasks with explicit units, settings ownership, bounded work, local approval and reliable recovery. Keep ordinary artist controls available.

3. Build a recipe library and artist review companion#

Extend the collection gallery and eight procedural examples with curated content and an artist review companion. Supported static asset packaging is explicit; arbitrary-terrain Paint transfer and additional renderer adapters remain separate work.

4. Prove personal learning and reference assistance#

Evaluate consented learning and reference-image suggestions against artist decisions and useful scene results before product integration.

5. Qualify studio workflows and wider delivery#

Validate representative hardware, renderers, deployment, recovery and licensing workflows before expanding supported delivery.

Reading the status labels#

Current means implemented within documented limits. Experimental means a bounded prototype. Planned means future work. A development version or successful test count is not general release certification.

documents.html:
Install a matching offline package#

MCP is a separate optional service. Install its matching offline package and the matching Scatter plugin, restart Max and run the supplied automation startup script. Scatter works without an assistant connection.

The MCP foundation remains independently versioned at 0.73.0. Its qualified authoring host is Max 2027; Scatter Max 2026 tests do not automatically qualify MCP on that host.

Enroll, review and apply#

Enroll an allowed site, mesh sources and planting regions. Read context, propose a supported plan, validate it and review the normalized settings in Max. Apply only the exact locally approved proposal.

Read-only inspection of an existing Scatter setup does not grant edit authority. Relevant scene changes require fresh context. Saving a result does not preserve permission for a later connection.

Tools and resources#

The interface supports connection/context inspection, plan validation, approved application, operation status, cached diagnostics/configuration/publication and bounded row reads. Viewport capture requires explicit sharing.

The control catalog describes more than the write API. Vector Paint Area authoring, containers, CS Edit mutation, complex terrain, map enrollment, renderer execution and ML are outside the current public authoring contract.

Bounds and supported semantics#

Design scopes allow up to three mesh sources, three regions/layers and 2,000 aggregate requested candidates. The supported site geometry is static, horizontal and convex; arbitrary modifiers and renderer proxies are not admitted design sources.

Lengths are metres, rotations degrees and scales multipliers. A request is a candidate budget, so spacing and masks can produce a shortfall. Unsupported fields fail explicitly.

Automation owns the objects it creates and cannot rewrite arbitrary artist objects. Local approval, scene freshness, ownership and bounded work apply to every supported mutation.

Diagnostics and recovery#

After an unknown operation outcome, query the existing operation rather than assume failure and retry blindly. Incomplete recovery blocks further writes.

Local recording is off by default and bounded. Recording does not grant sharing or training permission. Keep connection credentials private. The website itself does not connect to Max or collect scene telemetry.
